items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: he could do the drummer — Irv Cottler or somebody like that, and they’d have the beat going.

ctx.x: Yeah. In fact, many times he wasn’t on target, he would just quit. He would say, “Let’s cut it tonight” and then we’d go back the next night and start it again. His voice might have cracked or something. But he liked a lot of band because the band, I mean a live

band, because the band would kind of work him into it. But he was pretty strong on tempos. His tempo, Sinatra, you know he liked the two-four beat. When he would do that he would finally get the band because that wasn’t where Nelson would put it. You would see a night and day between the time we’d rehearse it with Nelson and then by the time Frank started singing it, he would start popping his finger, and he could do the drummer — Irv Cottler or somebody like that, and they’d have the beat going. So it would have…
It sounds like he learned it from Basie.
